ceos-motion.label: CEOS motion direction and animation engineering

routes.label: Creative concept
routes.secondaryContribution: Use Impeccable for a second-pass interface critique after CEOS establishes the concept direction.

routes.label: Art direction
routes.secondaryContribution: Use UI/UX Pro Max for palette and design-system references that support the approved art direction.

routes.label: Design research
routes.secondaryContribution: Use the CEOS reference catalog to find one relevant technique or skill after framing the research question.

routes.label: Typography and layout
routes.secondaryContribution: Use UI/UX Pro Max for stack-aware responsive typography and layout references after the type direction is set.

routes.label: Wireframes and user flows
routes.secondaryContribution: Use UI/UX Pro Max for targeted accessibility and interaction-pattern references after CEOS maps journeys and states.

routes.label: Motion direction
routes.secondaryContribution: Open GSAP guidance only if the approved motion spec needs its APIs; prefer CSS or WAAPI for simpler motion.

routes.label: GSAP implementation
routes.secondaryContribution: Use CEOS motion engineering to check intent, reduced-motion behavior, interruption, and cleanup around the GSAP code.

routes.label: React animations
routes.secondaryContribution: Use GSAP when its timeline or choreography adds value; simple UI state should use CSS or WAAPI.
routes.nonReactFallback: Use CSS or WAAPI for a simple headline; choose GSAP only if the motion needs a timeline.

routes.label: UI components and forms
routes.secondaryContribution: Use UI/UX Pro Max to check accessible behavior and interaction guidance for the selected component.
routes.nonReactFallback: Use semantic HTML forms and the native dialog element; follow existing project patterns if a custom dialog is needed.

routes.label: Creative interactive elements
routes.secondaryContribution: Use CEOS creative coding when an original Canvas, SVG, or WebGL visual is needed beyond a reusable interaction.
routes.nonReactFallback: Use semantic HTML and CSS or WAAPI for controls; use CEOS Creative Coding for an original Canvas or SVG interaction.

routes.label: Three.js and R3F
routes.secondaryContribution: Use CEOS realtime 3D to check scene lifecycle, rendering budgets, and fallbacks around the selected example.
routes.nonReactFallback: Use vanilla Three.js for an existing WebGL scene; use CSS or native interaction when a full 3D scene is unnecessary.

routes.label: GLSL and shaders
routes.secondaryContribution: Use pmndrs/examples only when the shader needs to integrate with an existing R3F scene or a tested example.

routes.label: Frontend architecture
routes.secondaryContribution: Use Superpowers TDD for narrow test-first checks after the architecture decision; keep orchestration with CEOS and the project policy.

routes.label: Complex implementation
routes.secondaryContribution: Use CEOS frontend architecture to check boundaries and state ownership while Superpowers stays within TDD.

routes.label: Debugging and verification
routes.secondaryContribution: Use existing project QA tools to reproduce and capture the failure; keep fault isolation under the project engineering workflow.

routes.label: Visual critique
routes.secondaryContribution: Use CEOS visual audit to record responsive evidence and prioritize concrete defects after the critique.

routes.label: Browser QA
routes.secondaryContribution: Use Superpowers verification to confirm requested browser evidence and clearly report checks that were not run.

routes.label: Performance
routes.secondaryContribution: Use existing measurement tools when they can collect the metric named by CEOS performance engineering.

routes.label: Release verification
routes.secondaryContribution: Use Superpowers verification to confirm release claims have recorded evidence without changing release authorization.

FAST.guidance: Make the named local change, inspect only the affected state or viewport, and run relevant checks. Skip concept options, owner approvals, signature-moment prototypes, and broad QA unless scope expands. Keep input validation, error handling, accessibility, keyboard/focus, reduced-motion, and security checks whenever the change touches them.
escalateWhen: The change affects behavior or multiple states
The scope expands beyond one local visual change
A new dependency or stack decision is needed
The work makes a brand-level direction choice

STANDARD.guidance: Use only the CEOS stages the task needs: frame it, research or set direction when useful, specify UX/motion/architecture when relevant, implement, inspect changed paths in a real browser, and verify relevant accessibility, performance, and security.
escalateWhen: The work is a launch or rebrand
Several routes need a shared visual system
An immersive signature moment needs a prototype
Several teams or stakeholders need approved handoffs

FLAGSHIP.guidance: Run the full CEOS path: reference research; distinct concepts and owner decision; art direction, UX, motion, and architecture as relevant; a desktop-and-phone signature prototype before bulk sections; build; responsive browser QA; independent visual, accessibility, performance, and security review; refinement; production-artifact and rollback verification.
